predictions.fixture: Gerwyn Price vs Rob Cross — PDC European Championship R1, Thursday 22 October, Westfalenhalle, Dortmund
predictions.text: Gerwyn Price to beat Rob Cross in Thursday's opening-night session at the Westfalenhalle in Dortmund is the selection, with the moneyline at our originated 1.47 the high-confidence play. The PDC's official draw seeds Price 13th against Cross in 20th on the one-year European Tour Order of Merit, and the tie is a rematch of the 2019 final, which Cross won — so the higher seed also carries a revenge motive into the match. At -213 in our book, Price to win is the pick.

predictions.fixture: Papua New Guinea vs Samoa — Men's Rugby League World Cup R2, Saturday 24 October, Santos National Football Stadium, Port Moresby
predictions.text: Samoa to win away to Papua New Guinea in Port Moresby on Saturday is the high-confidence selection, taking the moneyline at our originated 1.49. The NRL's official Round 1 reports show Samoa's record 78-4 rout of France at CommBank Stadium, with Sualauvi Fa'alogo scoring four tries off the bench — and Fa'alogo now starts after Deine Mariner's hamstring injury. Papua New Guinea beat Lebanon 42-18 on this same ground, a solid win but a level below a 74-point margin. Samoa's power and finishing make the visitors the clear pick.

predictions.fixture: Leinster vs Munster — United Rugby Championship R4, Saturday 24 October 13:00 local, Aviva Stadium
predictions.text: Leinster to win the derby against Munster at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday is the selection, backing the moneyline at our originated 1.51. The URC's official Round 3 centre has Leinster arriving in form after a 29-5 victory over Cardiff, while Munster were held to a 26-26 draw by Ulster. That gulf in recent scoring, plus home advantage at the Aviva for the stronger side right now, makes Leinster the high-confidence play.

predictions.fixture: New Zealand vs Cook Islands — Men's Rugby League World Cup R2, Sunday 25 October 4:05pm AEDT, One NZ Stadium, Christchurch
predictions.text: New Zealand to beat the Cook Islands in Christchurch on Sunday is the high-confidence selection, with the moneyline at our originated 1.55 the play. The NRL's official Round 1 wrap shows New Zealand pushing Australia all the way in a 24-22 instant classic at Allianz Stadium, while the Cook Islands trailed Fiji 28-0 at half-time on the way to a 40-12 defeat in Newcastle. Even with Kalyn Ponga sidelined by a broken arm and Valentine Holmes debuting for the visitors, New Zealand's class edge at home is clear: back the hosts to win.
